An AI that the SFC has registered for one or more regulated activities. The HKMA is the day-to-day frontline supervisor; ultimate responsibility stays with the SFC.
A firm licensed by the SFC for regulated activities. The joint circulars apply to LCs and RIs together as 'intermediaries'.
Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Among other roles, it grants stablecoin issuer licences under the Stablecoins Ordinance.
Securities and Futures Commission. It licenses VA trading platforms, and the Government proposes that it lead licensing and standard-setting for VA dealing and custody.
Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau. It issued Policy Statement 2.0 and runs the VA licensing consultations jointly with the SFC.
The HKMA's proposed role for banks under the coming VA dealing and custody regimes: it would supervise them, while the SFC sets the standards.
HKMA Supervisory Policy Manual module on supervising RIs' regulated activities. It is a statutory guideline under Banking Ordinance s.7(3).
A person an RI appoints, with the HKMA's written consent, to directly supervise a regulated activity. At least two are needed per activity.
The legal term, defined in s.53ZRA of the AMLO. Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) says the Government will now say 'digital assets' instead.
Covers VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets, and the keys, seeds and backups used to reach them.
VA service provider. The HKMA expects banks to assess each VASP customer's ML/TF risk on its own facts, with extra due diligence where needed.
VA trading platform. In SFC usage, a corporation licensed for Types 1 and 7 under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO), or holding an AMLO VA service licence.
A platform that was operating before 1 June 2023, met the deeming conditions and may keep operating while its licence application is decided. It is not licensed and may never be.
The 12-month window (1 June 2023 to 31 May 2024) in which pre-existing VATPs with a genuine Hong Kong presence could operate without breaching the AMLO licensing rule.
A wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary of a VATP that holds client assets on trust and does no other business.
Offline key storage. The SFC expects VATPs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage.

An SFC-approved arrangement a VATP should hold to cover potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot and other storage. For banks' custody, the HKMA's May 2026 guidance instead expects liability to clients plus adequate financial resources.
Defined in the SFO (Schedule 1, Part 1, s.1). Any other person is a 'retail client'.
A product that triggers the SFC's complex-product rules, including a suitability check even without a solicitation. VA-related products are very likely complex.
The SFC–HKMA circular on intermediaries' VA activities. The December 2023 version replaced those of January 2022 and October 2023, and was supplemented in September 2025.
Locking a client's VAs in a proof-of-stake network's validation to earn rewards.
An arrangement letting an SFC-licensed VATP pool orders with an overseas affiliate platform, using fully pre-funded orders and delivery-versus-payment settlement.
A leveraged VA derivative with no expiry. Under the SFC's February 2026 framework, licensed VATPs may propose them, and they should be offered to professional investors only.

glossary.def: Periodic payments between long and short holders of a perpetual contract that keep its price near spot. The SFC expects settlement at least once every 24 hours.

For banks, the HKMA Guideline sets customer due diligence for occasional VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more and points to AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A. RIs must also have regard to Chapter 12 of the SFC AML Guideline for VA provisions.

Software or hardware through which a person holds and moves VAs, keeping the private key themselves. The HKMA's May 2025 consultation proposed that licensed stablecoin issuers check whether a customer's wallet is custodial or unhosted.
A dedicated SFC list that helps the public spot suspicious platforms doing business in Hong Kong.
Under the June 2025 proposal, dealing in VAs as a business in Hong Kong, from simple conversion to brokerage and block trades. Banks would register with the SFC, with the HKMA as frontline regulator.

Under the December 2025 conclusions, safekeeping for others, as a business, the private keys or similar instruments that can move VAs. Trustees or managers that only delegate custody are out of scope.
Proposed regimes whose scope will match the SFO regimes for advising on securities (Type 4) and asset management (Type 9).
Automatic transitional licensing for incumbents. None is planned for the VA dealing or VA custodian regimes.
A faster approval track promised for SFC-licensed VATPs, and for LCs and RIs already providing VA dealing services.

A technology firm that splits control of private keys. Whether it needs a custodian licence is decided case by case, mainly on whether it can move client VAs on its own and whether clients can always reach their assets independently.
The February 2024 proposal for the Commissioner of Customs and Excise to license spot VA trading businesses, including shops and ATMs. The June 2025 dealing proposal revised it.
The law that set up licensing for regulated stablecoin activities. It commenced on 1 August 2025.
A stablecoin that references one or more fiat currencies. Issuing one in Hong Kong as a business, or issuing one that references the Hong Kong dollar anywhere, needs an HKMA licence.
A specified stablecoin issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer under its licence.
The HKMA's public list under s.21 of Cap. 656.
An HKMA arrangement launched in March 2024 to share supervisory expectations with would-be issuers. Admission was not an HKMA endorsement, and participants had to apply separately for a licence.
A digital representation of value that relies mainly on cryptography and DLT or similar technology, and can be used to pay, invest or access goods or services.

Tokenised traditional assets (1a) and stablecoins with effective stabilisation mechanisms (1b). Both carry the same capital requirements as the underlying traditional asset, plus any infrastructure add-on.
Unbacked cryptoassets, and tokenised assets or stablecoins that fail the classification conditions. They are fully capitalised; limited hedging is recognised for 2a and none for 2b.
HKMA non-statutory guidance on classifying cryptoassets. The Banking (Capital) Rules prevail if they differ.
LegCo's 28-day scrutiny of subsidiary legislation. The cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure-limit amendment rules completed it in August 2025.
A digital form of a commercial bank deposit, issued by the bank.
A DLT-based digital form of a real-world asset product that is not SFO-regulated (stablecoins excluded). The sales rules for the underlying product generally apply to its tokenised form.
A traditional security in a token wrapper. Its complexity is judged by looking through to the underlying security.
In Project Evergreen, a token minted by the CMU representing a claim on the HKMA for one Hong Kong dollar.
A bond first issued off the DLT platform and then tokenised on it. In Project Evergreen, CMU book entries came first and beneficial interests were then recorded on the ledger.
The Central Moneymarkets Unit. The HKMA owns it; CMU OmniClear Limited, a wholly owned Exchange Fund subsidiary set up in October 2024, operates it for the HKMA.
HKMA grant of up to HK$2.5 million per eligible digital bond issue in Hong Kong, open for an initial three years from November 2024.
An HKMA arrangement letting banks confirm DLT risk controls before a full launch, with optional live trials.
Distributed ledger technology. The HKMA's non-binding considerations expect an AI's board and senior management to take full responsibility for DLT risks.
Central bank digital currency; the e-HKD is the HKMA's possible digital Hong Kong dollar for wholesale and retail uses. The HKMA currently prioritises wholesale use.
Central bank digital money for settlement between banks, the basis of Project Ensemble.
The September 2024 renaming of Project e-HKD as it widened from the e-HKD alone to new forms of digital money, including tokenised deposits.
The HKMA's e-HKD path: foundations (Rail 1), use cases and pilots (Rail 2), implementation planning (Rail 3).
The HKMA project for tokenised-money settlement; EnsembleTX is its real-value pilot phase from November 2025.
An HKMA-formed group (May 2024) of regulators, banks and technology firms that develops industry standards for interoperability.
A multi-CBDC platform for real-time, 24/7 cross-border payment-versus-payment settlement.
On mBridge, banks meet each jurisdiction's KYC and AML/CFT rules outside the platform.

Payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment. The Ensemble Sandbox was built to test both for interbank settlement. The SFC describes DvP as a simultaneous exchange of assets that lowers non-delivery risk.
Settling both legs of a deal at the same instant, each leg depending on the other.

A 'wrapper' that sets conditions on how money is used while leaving the underlying value intact. Phase 2 pilots examined it as an alternative to a natively programmable e-HKD, which could weaken fungibility.
In Project Sela, a new kind of intermediary that provides customer-facing retail CBDC services, such as onboarding and KYC, without holding users' CBDC or its own liquidity.
A personal digital renminbi wallet opened with a Hong Kong mobile number, without real-name checks. Balance is capped at RMB10,000; retail payments only, no person-to-person transfers.
Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework: OECD standard for yearly automatic exchange of crypto-asset tax data.
Under the 2026 Bill, a business carrying out crypto exchange transactions for customers; 'HK' if it meets a Hong Kong nexus test.
Common Reporting Standard: the OECD model for yearly automatic exchange of financial account information (AEOI), which Hong Kong has run since 2018.
A reporting financial institution under the CRS. Under the amended CRS, RFIs report gross proceeds from sales of relevant crypto-assets by default.
Specified electronic money product: excluded from CARF but brought into the amended CRS.
Independent body to which, under the 2026 Bill, an RCASP could appeal a CARF financial-penalty assessment.
Customs' planned Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System and Anti-Money Laundering Analytics System (by 2029).
SFC initiative whose big-data market and AML surveillance parts are to switch on in 2027.
FATF's periodic report on how countries apply VA/VASP standards; the sixth was published on 26 June 2025.
The government's regulatory principle for VA activity since 2022.
Policy Statement 2.0's four areas: Legal streamlining, Expanding tokenised products, Advancing use cases, People and partnerships.
SFC 2025 roadmap: five pillars (Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure, Relationships) and 12 initiatives.
HKMA strategy with four pillars (data and payments, AI, resilience, tokenisation) and over 40 initiatives.
